calavera.setup:
Tío Rubén swore that mezcal “cleans the blood and calms the mind”;
La Catrina poured him six…
house: and found his mind — but lost his shoes, his keys and his spine.
his blood is very clean now. So is his bank account, she’d find.

calavera.setup:
My cousin’s ex showed up to the party with a brand-new date;
La Catrina took one look…
house: and said, “Mija, you upgraded. He downgraded. Isn’t that great?”
and seated them at the kids’ table, next to the piñata, by the gate.

calavera.setup:
La suegra came to visit “just a week” in 2011;
La Catrina came to fetch her…
house: and the husband offered help with the suitcases — all seven.
and the whole family lit a candle, thanking every saint in heaven.

calavera.setup:
Tía Coco had three husbands, and she outlived every one;
La Catrina asked her secret…
house: she said, “Separate bathrooms, mija — and a very good lawyer, hun.”
she winked and said, “Never marry a man who can’t make his own fun.”

calavera.setup:
Primo Julio’s dating profile said “six foot, loves to cook”;
La Catrina met him for a coffee…
house: he was five-foot-four, and “cooking” meant the microwave. Just look.
and swiped left in person. Twice. Just for fun.

calavera.setup:
Don Memo sneaked a tequila while his wife was saying grace;
La Catrina caught him…
house: and he toasted her with a perfectly straight face.
and his wife caught both of them. Catrina left the place.

calavera.setup:
At the wedding, Tía Linda caught the bouquet — at sixty-eight;
La Catrina was her plus-one…
house: and the whole room thought, “Well, she’s finally got a date.”
and caught the garter. They’ve been inseparable to date.

calavera.setup:
Tío Paco said, “I’m only having one,” at half past eight;
by midnight, La Catrina…
house: was driving him home, and he was proposing to the gate.
was the designated skeleton, and he was the freight.

calavera.setup:
My brother married someone who can’t cook, but she can dance;
La Catrina came for dinner…
house: and they ordered pizza. Then they danced. That’s romance.
and left hungry, but blushing, after one very long dance.

calavera.setup:
Cousin Vero swears her husband “doesn’t snore — he hums”;
La Catrina spent the night…
house: and the hum woke up the neighbours, and the dead, and drums.
and now she sleeps with earplugs, and with ear muffs, and with chums.

calavera.setup:
Tía Rosa’s mole recipe was guarded like a vault;
La Catrina tried to crack it…
house: and found the secret: love, chocolate and a fistful of salt.
and got chased out with a wooden spoon. Entirely her fault.

calavera.setup:
Abuelo bought a smart TV and asked it, “Where’s the news?”
La Catrina showed him buttons…
house: and he bought a radio. Problem solved. Nothing to lose.
and now he’s binge-watching telenovelas and refuses to choose.

calavera.setup:
The family dog sat by the ofrenda staring at the bread;
La Catrina turned around…
house: and the pan de muerto vanished — so did the dog, they said.
and found the dog had left an offering of his own instead.

calavera.setup:
My cousin brought a “healthy” dish to every family feast;
La Catrina tried a bite…
house: and returned to the grave to recover. At least.
it tasted like a yoga mat, and she’s a skeleton. That’s the least.

calavera.setup:
Papá took the family photo, and he only took one try;
La Catrina saw the picture…
house: and she was the only one whose eyes weren’t shut. Oh my.
it was mostly of his thumb, with a corner of the sky.

calavera.setup:
The kids built Catrina a skeleton from macaroni and glue;
when she saw her portrait…
house: she said, “It’s a perfect likeness. Is my hip really that blue?”
she hung it in the afterlife. It’s next to a Rembrandt. True.

calavera.setup:
Tío Fito lost the remote and blamed the ghosts again;
La Catrina checked the sofa…
house: and found it, plus nine pesos, three tamales and a pen.
and the ghosts said, “It wasn’t us.” It was Fito. Amen.

calavera.setup:
Abuela set the table for a hundred, just in case;
La Catrina counted heads…
house: there were seven. Abuela said, “Eat. You’re looking thin in the face.”
and stayed for seconds, thirds and fourths. Abuela set the pace.

calavera.setup:
My little sister painted sugar skulls with too much pink;
La Catrina saw the colours…
house: and changed her whole wardrobe. Pink suits her, don’t you think?
and needed sunglasses. She was blinded in a blink.

calavera.setup:
The neighbour’s rooster crows at three, at four, at five, at six;
La Catrina had a word…
house: and now he crows at noon. She taught the rooster some new tricks.
the rooster crowed at her. That’s how the feud began. It sticks.

loteria.verse:
I’m drawn on the napkin he slides to her drink;
I’m stolen at weddings, and broken — you think?
loteria.why: Doodled on napkins, stolen at weddings, broken after: the Heart.

loteria.verse:
I’m sung in the shower by men in their prime;
I serenade windows at quarter past time.
loteria.why: Shower singer and window serenader: the Musician.

loteria.verse:
I’m single, I’m sharp, and I’ve buried a few;
my love bites are lethal — I mean it, it’s true.
loteria.why: Single, sharp and famously deadly to her dates: the black widow.

loteria.verse:
He brought me on date one; on date ten, I was gone;
I came with the apology after he’d done wrong.
loteria.why: Date-one flowers and the classic apology bouquet: the Rose.

loteria.verse:
I’m asked for in marriage, then held at the altar;
I wander at parties — so watch me, don’t falter.
loteria.why: Asked for in marriage, held at the altar — and wandering at parties: the Hand.

loteria.verse:
I swim through the bars and I lure in the boys;
my song is a trap, and my tail makes no noise.
loteria.why: A siren song that lures the boys in: the Mermaid.

loteria.verse:
I’m dressed to impress, but my wallet’s on loan;
I flirt with your mother, then drive myself home.
loteria.why: All suit and no savings, flirting his way home: the Dandy.

loteria.verse:
I’m kicked off at midnight when the party is through,
and left by the bed — usually only one, too.
loteria.why: Kicked off after the party, one left by the bed: the Boot.

loteria.verse:
I sit on the altar with sugar for bones;
my forehead carries a name, not a phone.
loteria.why: Sugar skull with a name on its forehead: the Skull.

loteria.verse:
I’m a fruit and a feeling, I’m cut into slices;
I’m eaten in tacos and spared from the prices.
loteria.why: Sliced, grilled and tucked into tacos: the nopal.

loteria.verse:
I can hold up the sky, though I’m not very tall;
I come out when it’s pouring and hide in the hall.
loteria.why: It holds up the sky when it pours: the Umbrella.

loteria.verse:
I show you my face, but just one side, my dear;
I’m full once a month, and I never touch beer.
loteria.why: One face shown, full once a month: the Moon.

loteria.verse:
I strut through the yard in my red feather crown;
the whole village wakes when I sing them all down.
loteria.why: Red crown, morning alarm: the Rooster.

loteria.verse:
Lean me just right and I’ll help you get high —
the painter’s best friend, and a cat’s alibi.
loteria.why: Lean it right and it gets you high: the Ladder.

loteria.verse:
I’m a ring with no finger, a tongue with no taste;
I call you to weddings and parties in haste.
loteria.why: A ring with no finger and a tongue with no taste: the Bell.
